🌳 Learning

Decision tree

In simple words

A model that answers by asking a chain of yes/no questions about an example, like a flowchart.

A model that sorts an example by asking yes/no questions one after another (“Is it raining?”, “Is it warm?”) until it reaches an answer. The computer grows the tree from training examples, choosing at each step the question that splits them into the tidiest groups. Small trees are easy to read and check; very deep trees tend to overfit.

Example. A bank might use a decision tree to sort loan requests: “Has a steady income?” Yes → “Owes a lot already?” No → likely to pay back.

Related words

  • ModelA program that has learned patterns from data and uses them to make predictions or create something new.
  • OverfittingWhen a model memorises its training examples so closely that it does badly on new data.
  • Supervised learningLearning from examples that come with the right answers (labels).
  • Test setExamples put aside before training and used only to check how well a model does on data it has never seen.
